items.question: What risk arises when a translation layer between legacy and new domains has no owner for its mappings?

section_new.excerpt: ## Bounded pattern ownership notes ### Anti-Corruption Layer An anti-corruption layer is a translation boundary that keeps an external or legacy model from becoming the local authority. It owns mapping, validation and the explicit rejection of meanings that do not translate. The anti-corruption layer must maintain and monitor transaction and data consistency. It isolates the domain model from the external model and maps external concepts into the local domain language. The layer can become a single point of failure; plan for resilience with retry, circuit breaker, bulkhead and health endpoint monitoring. section_new.excerpt: ## 2. HTTP method semantics are not business-effect deduplication [RFC 9110, §9.2.1–9.2.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-9.2.2) defines the semantics of safe and idempotent methods. A safe method is intended not to request a state-changing effect. Idempotency describes the intended server-side effect of repeating an identical request; it does not require the responses, timing or logging events to be identical. PUT, DELETE and safe methods are idempotent by their specified semantics. POST has no general automatic-retry guarantee. Three distinct notions must not be merged: 1. **HTTP method contract:** Is the requested operation safe or idempotent according to its semantic

section_new.excerpt: ## Bounded pattern ownership notes These notes define the decision boundary for atlas cards whose mechanism is not the main subject of this page. They are synthetic design guidance, not measured evidence, and they do not create a new source claim. ### Cache Invalidation Cache invalidation removes a cached entry when the authoritative value changes, so a later read cannot reuse the superseded copy. On a write, write the change to the data store, then remove the affected cache entry. The next read repopulates the cache from the data store. This keeps the write path simple.
